bindings.label: Painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis for 1 month
Medical history includes elevated white blood cell count and inguinal lymphadenopathy discovered 9 years prior; 4 years after initial presentation, fatigue, weight loss, and loss of appetite occurred

Current illness began 1 month prior to admission with asymptomatic 'green-yellow welts' and swelling of the glans penis; swelling became progressively painful and evolved to the size of an 'orange' over 4 days
Previous treatments with topical antibiotics, antifungal agents, hydrogen peroxide soaks, warm compresses, and cephalexin showed no improvement

Physical examination: patient appeared healthy; glans penis and corona grossly edematous, with a 3.7 × 3.3-cm tender, firm ulcer on the ventral surface of the penis with overlying black eschar, adherent yellow crust, and granulation tissue; no urethral discharge
Penile ulcer biopsy shows dermal infiltrate of atypical CD20+/CD79a+/CD5+ B lymphocytes with clonal IgH rearrangement
PET-CT reveals FDG-avid abdominal and peripancreatic lymph nodes
Patient has systemic B-cell lymphoma, likely mantle cell lymphoma, with secondary penile involvement
Penile ulceration from secondary involvement by systemic mantle cell lymphoma (CD5+ B-cell lymphoma)
Penile ulceration from secondary involvement by systemic CLL/SLL (CD5+, CD23+ B-cell lymphoma)
Primary penile/cutaneous B-cell lymphoma (no systemic disease)
Penile ulceration due to a non-lymphoid penile malignancy (e.g., squamous cell carcinoma)
Cyclin D1, t(11;14)/CCND1 FISH, and SOX11 test results are not yet available
Pathologist reports penile gross and HE morphology are consistent with secondary lymphoma ulceration
